email.body1:
Paige, saw Ridgeline launched Intelligent Operations and its AI agents for investment management, with firms like Clarkston going live.

New products plus go-lives usually surface more in-market accounts than the team can cover, and that is where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so reps stop doing research and CRM work and spend time selling: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Ridgeline off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Paige, quick follow-up for Ridgeline.

As the platform expands, the list of investment firms worth working tends to outrun the team faster than expected. Most orgs don't know exactly how many meetings they need to hit target, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show how many meetings Ridgeline needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Paige, last bit of proof for Ridgeline.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks.

I pulled a benchmark of how Ridgeline's reply rate likely compares to peer fintech platforms. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Paige, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A product launch and new go-lives make for a busy stretch, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your sales motion? I will tailor it to Ridgeline either way.
